trial_court: Additional Sessions Judge, Junagadh at Porbandar in Criminal Appeal No. 6 of 1971
case_name: Mukta Jesing vs Vallabhadas Kalidas And Ors.
facts_of_case: Complainant Muktaben was the legally married wife of respondent No. 1. Their marriage had taken place according to Hindu religious rites and caste customs. Respondent No. 1 filed a suit for divorce, which was granted. During the pendency of an appeal against this decree, respondent No. 1 allegedly performed a second marriage with respondent No. 2 and others.

legal_principles.principle: A valid marriage between two parties must be proved by establishing that the marriage was performed according to Hindu rites and customs.
legal_principles.held: What was to be proved was that, but for the provisions of Section 17 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, which declares such second marriage to be void, there was a valid marriage between respondent No. 1 and respondent No. 2.

legal_principles.principle: An appeal under Section 417 of the Criminal Procedure Code will abate only on the death of the accused, not on the death of the appellant.
legal_principles.held: From this section it is clear that an appeal under Section 417 can only abate on the death of the accused and not otherwise.
cited_cases: Khedu Mohton v. State of Bihar

outcome.final_order: The trial court's order of acquittal was upheld, and the appeal was dismissed.
